system_overview: This specification models a simplified version of Leslie Lamport's Fast Paxos protocol, which extends classic Paxos to allow values to be learned in fewer message delays. The specification was written by Lim Ngian Xin Terry and Gaurav Gandhi, referencing Lamport's Fast Paxos paper and Zhao Wenbing's 'Fast Paxos Made Easy'. Fast Paxos introduces fast rounds where acceptors can propose values directly without the leader choosing a value, alongside classic rounds for collision recovery.
actors_and_components: The system has replicas (acceptors), a unique coordinator (leader), quorums (majority subsets), and fast quorums (larger subsets, at least three-quarters of the replicas). The coordinator is assumed to be unique, so Phase 1a and 1b of classic Paxos are omitted. All agents can communicate with one another.
state_variables: The system tracks six pieces of state: (1) the set of all messages sent, (2) the decided value (or a sentinel if no decision), (3) per-replica highest ballot seen, (4) per-replica highest ballot in which a value was accepted, (5) per-replica the value accepted in that highest ballot, and (6) a coordinator value tracking which value the coordinator has committed to (or a sentinel if none).
initial_state: Same as classic Paxos for the first five variables: empty message set, decision is the sentinel, all per-replica trackers at zero/sentinel. The coordinator value is also initialized to the sentinel.
actions: The protocol has six actions: (1) Fast Any (Phase 2a Fast): The coordinator starts a fast round by sending an accept-request message with the special 'any' value in a fast ballot. (2) Fast Propose (Phase 2b Fast): A replica receiving a fast-round accept-request (one containing the 'any' value) may respond with an acceptance message containing its own proposed value, provided the ballot is at least as high as its highest-seen ballot, it has not already responded to this ballot, and either it has not previously accepted a value or it accepts the same value. (3) Fast Decide: If all replicas in a fast quorum have sent acceptance messages in the same fast ballot and they all proposed the same value, that value is decided. (4) Classic Accept (Phase 2a Classic): If a fast round resulted in a collision (replicas in a fast quorum proposed more than one value), the coordinator selects a value for a classic round. If a majority of the fast quorum voted for one value, the coordinator must select that value. Otherwise, the coordinator may select any value from those proposed. The coordinator sends an accept-request with this value in a classic ballot numbered higher than the fast ballot. (5) Classic Accepted (Phase 2b Classic): Same as standard Paxos Phase 2b -- replicas accept the proposal if the ballot is high enough. (6) Classic Decide: If all replicas in a (classic) quorum accepted the same classic ballot, the value is decided.
safety_properties: Non-triviality: if a decision has been made, the decided value must have been proposed by some replica in a fast round (there exists an acceptance message for that value in a fast ballot). Type correctness: all variables have their expected types. Consistency: at most one value is ever decided.
liveness_properties: The specification includes strong fairness conditions on both Fast Decide and Classic Decide, ensuring that if deciding is repeatedly enabled, a decision is eventually made.
model_bounds: Four replicas, three values, ballot numbers from zero through four, fast ballots are a subset (for example, ballots one and three), classic ballots are the remaining ballots. Quorums are all majority subsets. Fast quorums are all subsets of size at least three-quarters of the replicas. Symmetry is exploited over replicas and values.
additional_assumptions: There is a unique coordinator, so Phase 1 is omitted entirely. All agents can communicate directly. Agent failures are modeled as pauses (agents restore from stable storage on restart). Fast quorums must be at least three-quarters of the replicas. Any classic quorum must overlap with the intersection of any two fast quorums. The fast ballot set and classic ballot set partition the full ballot set. A majority-value function determines whether a single value has majority support in a set of acceptance messages. The specification extends the companion classic Paxos module.
